NIA Resurrects Separatist Trio in 30-Year-Old Srinagar Violence Case

The National Investigation Agency (NIA) has filed charges against six Kashmiri separatist leaders, including Shabir Shah, in connection with a 1996 violence case in Srinagar. The move comes nearly three decades after the incident. The NIA claims that the accused were involved in planning and financing the unrest, which resulted in the deaths of several people. The chargesheet has been filed under various sections of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. The development has sparked concerns among separatist leaders and their supporters, who have accused the government of trying to silence them through legal action.
